transcript.text: My Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is sparking inside when I heat soup, little blue flashes on the right-hand wall and a crackling noise. I stopped it. Is it safe?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Stop using the microwave now: switch it off at the socket and unplug it, and don't run it again (not even empty) until we know why it sparked. Never take the outer casing off — parts inside can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged. Is it safe? No, it is not safe to use the microwave again until a qualified engineer has checked it. The sparking (arcing) can damage the internal components or cause a fire. Please do not try to run it again to test if it clears. To help identify what caused this, please switch off and unplug the appliance first. Then, look at the small rectangular cover panel on the inside right-hand wall (the waveguide cover). Is it burnt, holed, or discoloured? Also, check if there was any metal cutlery, foil, or a metallic-rimmed dish inside when this happened.

It's unplugged now. No metal or foil, just a plain plastic bowl of soup. The cardboard-like panel on the right wall has a black burnt spot with greasy splatter on it. There was a slight burnt smell and one wisp of smoke from that spot, which stopped when I turned it off.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. That suggests the likely cause: the small rectangular panel on the right wall (the waveguide cover or mica plate) has been damaged by arcing, which caused the spark, smoke, and burnt smell. Please do not attempt to fix this yourself or run the appliance to test it. You need a qualified engineer to replace the waveguide cover and inspect the interior for any other heat damage. Please contact Panasonic support or a local authorised repair service to arrange this.

candidates: Metal object or foil inside the cavity (high)
Burnt or damaged waveguide cover (mica panel) (medium)
